sentences.text: This crocodilian featured a blunt snout and back-jaw teeth designed to crush hard-shelled freshwater bivalves.
The animal reached a total length between 171.2 and 189.1 centimeters.
Scientists named the species in 2015 after finding fossils near Iquitos, Peru.
Fossil beds containing the bivalve genus Pachydon suggest these creatures fed on them in swamps and marshes.
It lived in the Amazon basin approximately 13 million years ago during the Middle Miocene.
This habitat was the Pebas Mega-Wetland System, a massive wetland covering over 1,000,000 square kilometers before the Amazon River Basin formed.
The species existed between 15.98 and 11.63 million years ago during the Langhian to Serravallian stages.
Researchers suggest that crushing dentition was an ancestral trait for the Caimaninae clade because basal members like Gnatusuchus and Globidentosuchus also possessed it.
